The existing tests cover many scenarios but maybe missing some exception cases: e.g., passing a TSIG object with null name, empty name, name with invalid format, algorithm not supported, secret null, error code invalid (maybe negative), querytsig when not appropriate, message already signed with TSIG already present and internal state inconsistent, message length exceeding MAXLENGTH causing WireParseException? Also could throw NullPointerException if key is null (already covered). Maybe IOException from TSIG processing (covered). Could also throw IllegalStateException if message is already signed and trying to set another TSIG while tsigState is intermediate? Not sure.

2. Passing TSIG with empty name (Name.root?) maybe invalid.

3. Passing TSIG with secret null -> maybe NullPointerException or IllegalArgumentException.

4. Passing TSIG with algorithm string null (covered). Already have null algorithm.

5. Passing TSIG with unsupported algorithm (e.g., "unknown-algo") -> may cause IllegalArgumentException or fail.

8. Passing a TSIG where secret length > 65535 causing message size overflow leading to WireParseException when later converting to wire; but setTSIG may not throw.

9. If Message already has a TSIGRecord but tsigState is TSIG_FAILED, calling setTSIG with valid key may cause IllegalStateException? Not sure.

10. If Message is null (calling on null) not relevant.
